steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Ahem. Citizens of Zeruertza, I am your environment and climate representative, Edge Eartheart.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: We are here today to discuss the future of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: The survey results are back, and the representatives have discussed a few possible solutions. We will make our choice from these options today.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: We also hope to come up with an answer for how the city will move forward.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: However, today's meeting will be officiated by Avdotya.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Are you sure about this, Avdotya?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Sure, you've lived in Zeruertza for quite a while, and the people in town know you. But this is the first time you'll be standing before everyone, right?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Alright, you're up, Avdotya.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I might take some time, Master Edge. Is that okay?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Don't worry, you won't break my record of putting half the city to sleep.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've never heard that story.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Oh, I remember. Master Eartheart went into a long discourse about geology.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: He went on and on until the sun went down, and only stopped when he wore himself out.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I probably won't go THAT long.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Go, Avdotya. This is the culmination of the time you spent here as our resident surface-born.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Thank you. Here goes.

steps.name: Voice from Far Away
steps.text: It's Avdotya!

steps.name: Voice from Far Away
steps.text: Avdotya! I'm with you, no matter what you say!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Why don't my speeches get the same reception?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: It's not just your record-breaking speech. All the other meetings you officiate last for ages.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I know you're always the first to fall asleep.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Not today. Avdotya looks different this time. What does she have on her mind?

steps.name: Excited Durin
steps.text: Fantastic. I respect Master Edge's knowledge, but his meetings are torturous.

steps.name: Relaxed Durin
steps.text: Avdotya's voice is as beautiful as she is. I could listen to her all day.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Greetings, citizens of Zeruertza. I am Avdotya, literature representative.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Today, I officiate over this meeting that will determine Zeruertza's future.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: We have discussed with Master Edge and believe that there are three practical plans to carry out Zeruertza's evacuation.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Before discussing the plans, however, there's something else that I want to talk about.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It's about my past.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Not the past of Avdotya Razorpen, but the past of Avdotya Nikolayevna Ivanova.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: When I first came to live among the Durins, I created many stories, and shared mine with many people.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This, however, I've never told anyone.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I want to share it with you today.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I was born to a noble family in Ursus.
Avdotya thought she would struggle to find words.
But she found her memories pouring out as soon as she opened her mouth.
It was not that she did not know what to say; it was that she had too much to say and did not know where to start.
The Durins do not know what it means for her. But she does.
This is the first time she's looked back on her past since coming to the Durins.
She thought time would let the past fade, let her forget that she was once a woman of Ursus.
Now, though, she realizes that the past never truly goes away.
But meeting Gavial and the people she brought with her helps her realize—
That is not so bad.
The past pulls her down bit by bit, along with the Durins listening to her story.
But she no longer feels pain from it, and thus neither do the Durins.
Stitch sits in his room, trying not to think about it.
But he can't help it.
He knows this is his last chance.
Let it go, and he will never surpass his teacher.
And he has a feeling that if he does not win this time, he will always be second-best, though to what he cannot describe.
He knows.
But he can't do it.
He puts his arms around his head.
Knock knock.
There is someone knocking on his door.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Stitch, you're here, right?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I know you're in there.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Leave me alone, Gavial!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: We need to talk.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Talk to Catch if this is about the dome.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No can do.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Because this is your job.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Open the door.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're not coming in here!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: That's not up to you.
The door and the walls around it collapse with a bang, and Gavial walks in casually holding her great axe.
She sees Stich sitting by the desk with his arms around his head, his expression hidden.
A few blank pieces of paper lie by his hand.
A few more pieces of paper lie by his feet, either torn to pieces or crumpled up.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Design sketches for the dome.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You wanted to do it, didn't you?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Can't you give me a break, Gavial?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It's not so much that I'm not giving you a break...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Look at you, shutting yourself in this room staring at sketches, holding in everything you're thinking.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You're the one who's not giving yourself a break, Stitch.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You don't know anything...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Right, which is why I'm not taking you back by force.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I don't know. So I gotta find out.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why did you smash my door then?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You wouldn't have talked if I didn't.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're just threatening me...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm a reasonable woman. I could even be convinced to help you, if you have a good enough reason.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I realized something, on my way over here

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You weren't happy with the whole dome repair thing, were you? From the very beginning?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Life on the surface can be so colorful. I never heard Avdotya talk about it... right, Master Edge?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Huh? Mm.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: It's nothing. Rare to see you drift off like this, though. What's the matter?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I was thinking about Stitch.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Stitch? Aren't Gavial and Catch looking for him? Ought to be fine, right?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: The question isn't fine or not.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Seeing him today made me realize I may have pushed him too hard without realizing.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: You're talking about the dome repair?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Of course, I was in agreement about not repairing the dome.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But I was also anxious about the broken survey equipment.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You know how Stitch has been since his teacher went missing.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: He submitted a series of proposals for the dome that got rejected. At some point he stopped coming to design meetings, shuttering up in his room.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I thought I could push him a little... if he could come up with a new plan to repair the dome, it would be an opportunity to bring it up.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I could help him.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: He ended up going up to get surface-dwellers to fix the railway.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Yeah, I didn't expect him to go this far to avoid fixing the dome.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: So I thought, forget it, the Originium vein takes priority.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: If he's so reluctant to repair it, just let it be; there will be more chances in the future.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Little did I know there would be no more chances.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: This isn't your fault. If anything, it's Stitch's for running away.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But if this dome is so important to him—

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: He'll regret it for the rest of his life, if he doesn't seize the opportunity.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why are you so against repairing the dome?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Because of the job my teacher left me.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Teacher? Job? Didn't Catch say your teacher went missing?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: It wasn't... a sudden disappearance.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Though he didn't tell anyone else, he did leave me an assignment.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I have to win everyone over with my dome design, and make the dome of Zeruertza my own.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Only then will he come back to find me.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Otherwise, he'll never come back.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Your last name is Canvas too. Are you related?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No, I changed it later.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Eight years ago, I survived an Originium vein explosion. I had no home to return to, but my teacher took me in.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So your Oripathy...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Yes, that was when I caught it.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: On the surface, people with this disease are called the Infected and cast out from society.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: That's not the case among the Durins, but we can't fully cure it, only keep its symptoms in check.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It's the same up there.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: So I changed my name to that of my mentor and studied architecture under him.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I hear he was pretty famous?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Of course! Finch Canvas was the design representative of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Surface-dwellers would call our style 'minimalist'.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: We oppose elaborate and flashy designs, seeing them as the unchecked spread of desire, the product of a slothful life.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: At this rate, we will inevitably be swallowed up by our own desire.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: That's why we advocate a lifestyle that emphasizes the true nature of things.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: True nature?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: How things are in their most natural state. We oppose all unnecessary functions, trying to keep things the way they are.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: This is our rebellion against a life of desire.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Like the simple design of your room?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No, my style is not exactly the same as that of my teacher.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: My style came from his, but in some ways, we go in opposite directions.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Allowing the city to welcome destruction while looking its best is a luxury that comes only from our excess productivity. It is arrogant and wasteful.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: One's time is limited, and my clock is ticking!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're Infected too, Gavial. Don't you understand?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You only have so much time left. You need to spend your efforts on something more meaningful.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Of course. That's why I study medicine, so I can heal myself and people like me.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But if that's how you feel, why not seize this last chance?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You think I don't want to?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Do you see the sketches here?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: They are proof of my failure over the years!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I made proposal after proposal, only to see all of them rejected!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: After that, I couldn't even come up with a passable sketch.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I don't know who is the problem: the Zeruertzans, or me.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: All I know is that the mere sight of the dome fills me with fear.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: It's like a cage that my teacher has locked me in, trapping me forever.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Even if it's my last chance.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I can't do it anymore!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Even if I came up with a new plan, there's no hope of it getting through.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: And you tell me how I'm going to come up with a new plan that can pass review in such a short time?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'm not coming with you, Gavial.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'm a failure.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Tell Master Edge that if he wants the dome fixed, he can have Catch do it.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: He'll undoubtedly do a better job than I can.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright, I get it now.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: All the more important for you to come with me.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Haven't you been listening?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But you're the one who's got to explain it to the gang.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Strange Machine A
steps.text: Stitch is in danger. Stitch is in danger.

steps.name: Strange Machine B
steps.text: Protect Stitch. Protect Stitch.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hey, where did these bots come fr—

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Stop right there!
